summary: Lassen County lookout north of Eagle Lake: the register dates it 1973, but a 1937 CCC project and a 1946 staffing item predate that; still manned per a 2023 local history.

facts.design: Steel-pipe corner posts with angle iron, H-bracing and cable X-bracing; the first of five towers of this design; cab designed by CDF engineer Mike Plesha
facts.agency: California Department of Forestry and Fire Protection, Lassen-Modoc Unit (Cal Fire LMU)

visit.trail_note: Reached by a dirt road, per Wikipedia; the sources read do not say whether the public may visit

events.note: Local history says the Lassen County supervisors sought a lookout in spring 1937; the Secret Valley CCC camp was to supply labor, and the history says the job got done; the register gives 1973
June 1946 newspaper item: a lookout had been stationed on Fredonyer peak
Photograph of the Fredonyer lookout taken in 1952, from the California Division of Forestry Black Cards collection
Time-lapse camera installed at the lookout in a State Forestry and Weather Bureau study; a radar system for lightning warnings was set up around then
CAL FIRE 2011-2012 plan added Fredonyer Peak to its list of historic buildings to preserve, in place of Dyer Mountain; the state owns and controls it
Register: staffed by Bureau of Land Management observers as of 2015
September 18, 2023 local history says the lookout is still manned

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register gives 1973. A 2023 local history says the Lassen County board sought a lookout in 1937 and the Secret Valley CCC camp was to supply labor, with the job getting done; a June 1946 item says a lookout was already stationed on the peak. A 1952 photograph also shows a lookout. The story reports the disagreement and does not pick a single date.

notes_for_editor: Build date is unresolved: the 1973 register date may refer to a later tower, since the register's design note cites a 1991 test period (MVT 10/91), but no source read confirms that. Editor may want a 1937 or 1946 event after review. Current staffing: the register says BLM observers staffed it as of 2015, and the 2023 local history (dated September 18, 2023 in the page's HTML; the date is not in the text extract, so it is not an evidence quote) says it is still manned. Access: no source read says whether the public may visit; the site is a state-owned working lookout, so check with CAL FIRE before relying on any visit. A CAL FIRE fact sheet (PDF, undated) lists Fredonyer Peak Lookout as a Lassen-Modoc unit lookout and says such lookouts are usually staffed only in peak season; it was not cited in the story. The 1952 Knedler photo is a public archive item, but its licence was not checked, so it is not added to photos. The 2011-2012 plan note ties Fredonyer's preservation status to Dyer Mountain, see the Dyer story.
